summary: The NL Scholarship (formerly the Holland Scholarship) is paid by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science together with participating Dutch research universities and universities of applied sciences. It is for students from outside the European Economic Area who will study a full-time bachelor's or master's programme at a participating institution. The award is EUR 5,000, paid in the first year of study, and the official page says it is not a full-tuition scholarship. The scheme is run institution by institution: each participating university or university of applied sciences sets its own application, selection, deadline and eligible programmes.
eligibility_notes:
The national rules on the official page are four: the applicant has a non-EEA nationality; applies for a full-time bachelor's or master's programme at a participating institution; meets the specific requirements of that institution; and does not already hold a degree from a Dutch education institution.

Because each institution runs its own selection, the extra rules differ. The institution pages read show these examples. University of Groningen: no EEA nationality (Swiss and Surinamese nationals are listed as not eligible), excellent bachelor's grades, an admission offer for a listed programme, no earlier NL Scholarship; it is awarded for one year, once only. University of Twente: master's students only, a CGPA of 7.5 out of 10 (about the top 5 to 10 percent of the graduating class), admission to a qualifying master's programme, English language requirements met, not eligible for a Dutch study grant, and not paying the statutory (EU/EEA level) tuition fee. Utrecht University: master's applicants who are not eligible for the Dutch study grant and loan system or the statutory tuition fee, who have never been enrolled at a Dutch educational institution, and who applied to a participating international master's programme. Radboud University: a non-EU/EEA passport, an English-taught master's programme (Erasmus Mundus and joint degrees excluded), a bachelor's degree from outside the Netherlands, and a combined application with the university's own scholarship programme; the NL Scholarship cannot be awarded alone.

The official page does not list the EEA countries. It does not list required documents; those are set by each institution.
age_experience_notes: No age limit or work experience requirement is stated on the official scheme page or on the four institution pages read.
funding_summary: EUR 5,000, paid in the first year of study. It is not a full-tuition scholarship and does not cover living costs in full. Institution pages read say it is paid once for one year, even for two-year master's programmes (Utrecht, Radboud, Groningen, Twente). Groningen pays it in instalments after arrival; other pages do not say how it is paid. Utrecht's page lists award amounts of EUR 5,000, 10,000 or 15,000, which differs from the national figure.
programmes_note: Full-time bachelor's or master's programmes at participating institutions. The scheme page names no fields and says each institution lists its own fields of study for the year. Examples of the variation: Twente lists 29 master's programmes (for the 2027/2028 intake); Radboud limits the scheme to English-taught master's programmes and gives a fixed number of awards per faculty; Utrecht says not every programme takes part and tells applicants to check the financial support section of each programme page.
institutions_note: The Study in NL page for the 2027-2028 round lists 33 participating institutions: 10 research universities and 23 universities of applied sciences or arts. The earlier 2026-2027 listing stored by SAS counted 11 research universities, and the list changes every year. Research universities on the 2027-2028 list: Eindhoven University of Technology, Maastricht University, Protestant Theological University, Radboud University, University of Groningen, University of Twente, Utrecht Theological University, Utrecht University, VU Amsterdam, and Wageningen University & Research. A student chooses an institution, applies for admission there, and then applies for the scholarship through that institution. Each institution sets its own closing date, selection criteria and eligible programmes.

summary.detail: Full-time bachelor's programmes at participating institutions, with the institution's own entry requirements. The institution pages read (Twente, Utrecht, Radboud) describe the scholarship for master's students only; Groningen lists bachelor's programmes but describes the award for master's study. The scheme page does not say which institutions offer it at bachelor's level.
Full-time master's programmes at participating institutions, with the institution's own entry requirements. Programmes that take part are chosen by each institution.

benefits.limit_text: EUR 5,000, paid in the first year of study
benefits.conditions: Not a full-tuition scholarship. Paid once for one year. At Groningen it is paid in instalments after arrival in the Netherlands. At Twente it is meant to compensate study-related costs and tuition is not paid on the student's behalf. The scholarship stops if the student becomes eligible for the statutory tuition fee (Twente).

benefits.limit_text: Not a full-tuition scholarship; the EUR 5,000 is a fixed sum
benefits.conditions: Twente says tuition is not paid on the student's behalf; the scheme page does not say how the sum may be used.

requirements.text: The scheme page gives no document list. The student applies for admission to the chosen institution first and then follows that institution's scholarship application, with its own documents.
Motivation letter explaining why you are the right candidate (University of Groningen; Utrecht and Radboud also judge motivation).
requirements.conditional_rule: Where the institution asks for it

requirements.text: Transcript of the undergraduate courses taken so far, and the admission offer letter (University of Groningen).
requirements.conditional_rule: Where the institution asks for it

requirements.text: Statement of Financial Resources on the university's form, plus the scholarship form in the online application portal (Utrecht University).
Proof of English proficiency required by the chosen programme (Radboud University recommends sending it before its completeness deadline).

application_steps.title: Choose a participating institution and programme
application_steps.detail: Check that your nationality is non-EEA, that you do not hold a Dutch degree, and that the institution and programme take part. Participating institutions change every year; the Study in NL page lists 33 for the 2027-2028 round.

application_steps.title: Apply for admission to the programme
application_steps.detail: You normally need to have applied to, or been admitted to, the programme before the scholarship application. Groningen requires an admission offer; Twente says apply to the master's first and then submit the scholarship form with your student number; Utrecht requires an application to an eligible master's programme first.

application_steps.title: Submit the institution's scholarship application
application_steps.detail: Each institution has its own form, documents and closing date; check its scholarship page. Examples: Groningen asks for a motivation letter and the admission letter; Utrecht asks for an online form and a Statement of Financial Resources; Radboud takes the request inside its online application and combines it with its own scholarship programme. Incomplete applications are not considered (Groningen, Radboud).

application_steps.title: Institution ranks the applications
application_steps.detail: There is no national selection. Each institution ranks applicants itself. Examples: Groningen ranks complete applications on academic merit and the motivation letter; Utrecht judges academic background, motivation and the quality of a financial plan; Radboud faculty committees judge academic excellence and ambition, with a fixed number of awards per faculty.

application_steps.title: Wait for the institution's decision
application_steps.detail: Results come from the institution. In the pages read, results are announced in the weeks after the closing date (Utrecht expects mid-April, Twente the first week of May, Radboud mid-April). Admission and scholarship selection are separate decisions; being admitted does not mean you receive the scholarship.

application_steps.title: Receive the EUR 5,000 in your first year
application_steps.detail: The award is paid in the first year of study, once, for one year. Groningen pays in instalments after you arrive in the Netherlands. You must still be able to get a Dutch student visa where that applies, and must meet the institution's enrolment conditions. Twente cancels the award if you become eligible for the statutory tuition fee.

Institution pages show the 2027-2028 intake (and one Radboud passage still mentions 2026-2027), so their dates and quotas are not those of the 2026-2027 round stored by SAS.
